title: add-tenant-metadata-module-and-network-handoff-for-gpu-lease-coordination
author: Asha Patel
release_notes: Introduces a tenant_metadata terraform module and a network handoff pattern for private installs. Enables immutable-lease annotations on GPU node pools and reduces cross-tenant tfstate coupling. No behavioral changes to runtime; ops must run the included migrator when upgrading.
description:
Motivation: Private deployments need an explicit, auditable tenant metadata surface that plays well with multi-tenant VPC handoffs and GPU lease orchestration. Historically tenant identity and network claims were embedded in ad-hoc TF snippets tied to cluster tfstate which caused cross-tenant state coupling, painful upgrades, and race conditions during tenant handoff.

This PR adds a dedicated `tenant_metadata` Terraform module and a lightweight `network_handoff` helper that standardizes how tenant-level network claims (VPC/subnet/peering) are recorded and later consumed by the private-installer controllers. The module is intentionally small: it writes immutable metadata, exposes stable outputs for claim lookup, and emits annotations consumed by the GPU lease reconciler. The handoff flow also includes a small migrator plan to move existing tenant claims out of shared tfstate into tenant-scoped state files.

What changed (high level): commit summaries below and a short list of changed files. The PR touches TF modules, Helm values shipped by the installer, a small kubectl job used during migration, and added unit/plan tests for the module. CI run passed after one flaky plan test was retried. Reviewers requested and we added explicit locking guidance and a rollback-safe migrator. The PR was squash-merged into main.

Notes about upgrade: Operators must run the provided `tfstate-migrate` plan (scripts/migrate_tenant_metadata.sh) when moving from releases older than 2025-11. The migrator is opt-in; failing to run it will keep behavior compatible but operators will not benefit from the improved isolation and will continue to see tenant metadata in the previous state location.

Commits summary: This is a single squashed merge comprised of the following logical commits: 1) create modules/tenant_metadata with inputs (tenant_id, owner_contact, intent) and outputs (metadata_ref, network_claims_ref); 2) add modules/network_handoff to record VPC/subnet/peering claims and emit handoff annotations; 3) hook module outputs into helm values via installer/templates/values-tenant-metadata.yaml; 4) add scripts/tfstate-migrate helper and a deterministic rollback marker; 5) tests: terraform unit plan tests and an integration plan that runs against a small local backend; 6) docs: docs/private/tenant-metadata.md and upgrade notes in CHANGELOG.

Changed files (high-level): ["modules/tenant_metadata/main.tf", "modules/tenant_metadata/outputs.tf", "modules/network_handoff/main.tf", "installer/helm/values-tenant-metadata.yaml", "helmcharts/private-installer/templates/deployment.yaml", "scripts/tfstate-migrate.sh", "docs/private/tenant-metadata.md", "tests/terraform/tenant-metadata-plan.test", "Makefile (new target: tfstate-migrate)", "examples/private/tenant-claim-example.tf", "README.md (installer section updated)", "ci/plan-checks.yaml"].

Review conversation (highlights): - Diego: "Can we guarantee the handoff annotations are idempotent if a second reconcilation runs mid-migration?"; Asha: "Yes — annotations are computed from the module output which is based on a tenant metadata hash; the migrator writes an immutable marker to prevent second-run race conditions. Added a unit test that retries annotation writes and asserts idempotency." - Linnea: "We need clearer operator guidance for state locking and lock TTLs for cross-account runs."; Asha: "Added section in docs and a Makefile target that calls `terraform init -lock-timeout=10m` and a recommended runbook snippet." - Evan: "Edge-case: existing tenants with partial network claims (only VPC but not peering) — how do we handle reconciliation?"; Asha: "The handoff module emits a `claim_status` map which the installer controller will treat as 'partial' and schedule a follow-up reconcile; I added tests to simulate partial claims and a note in the operator docs." - Security review (SRE): "Ensure sensitive values are stored only in encrypted backends"; Asha: "Tenant secrets are not stored in plaintext; module is written to expect encrypted backend or use provider-managed secrets (SSM/KMS). Documented provider requirements."

CI summary: GitHub Actions pipeline ran `terraform fmt` (pass), `terraform validate` across modules (pass), `unit plan tests` (pass), `integration plan` (flaky - one retry required, then pass), `helm lint` (pass), `installer e2e smoke` (skipped in CI for speed). One flaky test (tests/terraform/tenant-metadata-plan.test) failed on the first run due to local backend timing; rerun passed. All checks green at merge time.

Migration and rollback: The included `scripts/tfstate-migrate.sh` does a conservative three-way merge with locks and writes a rollback marker file in the old state bucket. Rolling back is supported by the marker and a helper `scripts/tfstate-rollback.sh` that reimports state chunks. Documented steps in docs/private/tenant-metadata.md.

Merge: Squash merged into main by Linnea Sørensen on 2026-03-03 (merge method: squash).
